exercises.title: U5 听力·对话 Choosing a First-Aid Skill
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Lucy: Our school is offering a first-aid club. Which skill do you want to learn most, Tom?
Tom: I want to learn how to help a choking person. My uncle once choked on a fish bone.
Lucy: That sounds really useful. I'd like to learn how to treat burns.
Tom: Why burns?
Lucy: My little sister once burnt her hand on a hot pan, and I didn't know what to do.
Tom: I see. Then this club is perfect for both of us.
Lucy: Yes. The teacher said we will also learn how to call for an ambulance.
Tom: Great. Let's sign up together after class.
exercises.translation_cn: Lucy 问 Tom 最想学哪项急救;Tom 想学帮噎住的人,因为叔叔曾被鱼刺噎住;Lucy 想学处理烧伤,因为妹妹曾被热锅烫伤而自己不知所措;两人决定一起报名,还会学怎么叫救护车。

exercises.title: U5 听力·短文 Emergency Numbers
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Different countries use different emergency phone numbers.
In China, you can call one-two-zero for an ambulance.
In the United States, people call nine-one-one for any emergency.
In the United Kingdom, the number is nine-nine-nine.
When you call, stay calm and tell the operator clearly where you are and what has happened.
exercises.translation_cn: 不同国家有不同的急救电话:在中国拨120叫救护车;在美国拨911处理任何紧急情况;在英国是999;打电话时要保持冷静,清楚地告诉接线员你在哪里、发生了什么。

options: All countries use the same number.

options: Shout as loud as you can.

questions.stem: What two things should you tell the operator?
options: Where you are and what has happened.

exercises.title: U5 听力·对话 A Friend Gets Burnt
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Mark: Anna, come quick! I burnt my arm on the cooker!
Anna: Stay calm, Mark. Let me see. It's red but not too deep.
Mark: It really hurts. Should I put some butter on it?
Anna: No, never put butter on a burn. That keeps the heat in.
Mark: So what should I do?
Anna: Hold your arm under cool running water for about ten minutes.
Mark: That feels much better already.
Anna: Good. Then we'll cover it loosely with a clean cloth. If it gets worse, we'll go to hospital.
exercises.translation_cn: Mark 在灶台上烫伤了胳膊,慌忙叫 Anna;Anna 让他冷静,查看后说不深;Mark 问能否抹黄油,Anna 说绝不能,会把热留住;她让他把胳膊放凉水下冲约十分钟,Mark 感觉好多了;之后用干净布宽松地盖住,若加重就去医院。

options: It keeps the heat in the burn.

exercises.title: U5 听力·短文 The Heimlich Manoeuvre
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: The Heimlich manoeuvre is a simple way to help a person who is choking.
First, make sure the person really cannot speak or breathe.
Stand behind the person and wrap your arms around the waist.
Make a fist and push up into the stomach with quick movements.
Keep doing this until the food is forced out and the person can breathe again.
exercises.translation_cn: 海姆立克急救法是帮助噎住者的简单方法:先确认对方确实说不出话、不能呼吸;站到其身后,用双臂环住腰;握拳并用快速动作向上推压腹部;持续进行,直到食物被推出、对方重新能呼吸。

options: You push up into the stomach.

questions.stem: When do you stop?
options: When the food is forced out and the person can breathe.

exercises.title: U5 听力·对话 A 999 Call
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Operator: Emergency services. What is your emergency?
Boy: My grandfather has fallen down and he isn't moving!
Operator: Stay calm. Is he breathing?
Boy: I'm not sure. He looks very pale.
Operator: All right. Put him on his back and remove any pillows.
Boy: Okay, I've done that.
Operator: Now put your hand in the middle of his chest and press down, twice a second.
Boy: I'm pressing now. Please send someone quickly!
Operator: An ambulance is already on the way. Keep going until it arrives.
exercises.translation_cn: 接线员问发生了什么;男孩说爷爷摔倒了,不动了;接线员让他冷静,问是否在呼吸;男孩说不确定、爷爷脸色很苍白;接线员指导他让爷爷仰卧、移开枕头,把手放在胸部中央每秒按压两次;男孩照做并请求快点派人;接线员说救护车已在路上,让他坚持到车来。

exercises.title: U5 听力·短文 Three Rules of First Aid
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Here are three simple rules to remember when you give first aid.
First, stay calm and do not panic, even if the person is badly hurt.
Second, make sure that the place is safe before you help.
Third, call for help early, and never be afraid to ask for an ambulance.
If you follow these rules, your quick action may save someone's life.
exercises.translation_cn: 给急救时要记住三条简单原则:第一,保持冷静、别惊慌,哪怕伤者伤得很重;第二,在施救前确认现场安全;第三,尽早求助,别害怕叫救护车。遵守这些原则,你的迅速行动也许能救人一命。
